transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I forgot something important. Like maybe I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or didn’t set up my classroom materials safely. Even when I know I probably did everything right, the doubt just keeps coming back.
When you have these doubts about forgetting something, do you find yourself doing things like double-checking, re-reading instructions, or asking others for reassurance to make the worry go away?

Yes. Before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll check the same things a few times—the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans. Sometimes I just replay what I did in my head until I feel calm enough to leave. I know it can be excessive, but otherwise I keep worrying, and it does make me late sometimes.

When these thoughts about forgetting something pop into your mind, do they feel like unwanted, intrusive thoughts that you wish would just go away, or do they feel more like your normal way of worrying about things?
They feel unwanted. I’ll know I probably handled it, but then the thought that I forgot something—like my aunt’s medicine or classroom materials—just keeps popping back into my head anyway.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling down, or a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
No, I haven’t really noticed feeling down or losing interest in things I usually enjoy.

Aside from these thoughts about forgetting things or making mistakes, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of other different areas of your life, like health, finances, or family, in a way that's hard to control?
I don’t think so. It’s mostly these specific worries about forgetting something or making a mistake, not a lot of different things all at once.
